steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Block printing uses carved stamps applied to fabric; screen printing forces ink through a mesh stencil — both can create repeat patterns. | Key Fact: Batik applies wax as a resist before dyeing — the wax blocks dye, creating patterns where the wax is removed. | Key Fact: Tie-dye and shibori create patterns through resist: binding, folding, twisting or compressing fabric before dyeing. | Key Fact: Repeat patterns use a single motif repeated systematically — half-drop, brick, mirror and random repeats create different visual effects.
